sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: The source proves the marked-piece bound for every finite connected loopless edge set, with a separate finite-tree specialization. It preserves edge and endpoint coverage; marked endpoints may be shared between pieces.

sourceOccurrences.label: Power-law bootstrap and critical endpoint
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2008.11197v2, Proposition 1.4, Lemma 4.1, Theorems 1.1–1.2, Remark 1.3; printed pp. 2–4, 8–10, 28–31
sourceOccurrences.note: The lattice and weight-threshold arguments retain the A-squared two-cluster estimate, finite susceptibility below the threshold, finite-star proof of a finite critical parameter and finite-witness critical passage. The elementary contraction is supplied separately with a weaker numerical two-ghost constant. The group-kernel construction is included. The two intermediate-power discrepancies were also checked in the publisher HTML; full journal-edition reconciliation and formal correspondence remain separate.

sourceOccurrences.label: Infinite-graph marked partition
sourceOccurrences.locator: Lemma 2.4, arXiv:2008.11197v2 and publisher HTML, Section 2.1
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Finite-core extension of the corrected partition
sourceOccurrences.note: Partition a finite spanning subtree of the marked vertices by DMI0, then attach each unmarked complementary branch to an incident piece. All vertices are covered, the strict marked-mass bounds persist, and on a tree all edges are partitioned. Infinite pieces are not treated as finite BK witnesses.

sourceOccurrences.label: Spatial-average volume-tail transfer
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:2202.07634v2 §3, (3.1)–(3.6), compared with the general deduction GW20
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Written deduction with existing probability inputs
sourceOccurrences.note: A general transfer is proved with arbitrary spatial-sum exponent gamma<d. It reuses the written two-ghost theorem, chooses the radius directly from n, and solves a finite least-amplitude quadratic. No imported two-ghost theorem is needed.

sourceOccurrences.label: Norm tightness
sourceOccurrences.note: 3109 extends the existing DMI0/12NL proof to every norm, retains isolated marks, handles countable witnesses and atomic quantiles, and gives explicit constants.

sourceOccurrences.label: Fixed-index moment control
sourceOccurrences.note: 25TW proves the moment and mixed-moment estimates with exponent-dependent constants. The source uniform-index claim has a counterexample within a fixed critical hierarchical model.

proofUses.reason: Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz, Harris and the balanced lattice radius give the amplitude contraction.
Subcritical finite susceptibility, the best admissible amplitude, finite stars and finite witnesses close the critical theorem.
A lower bound on the edge-weight counting function replaces the Euclidean annulus; summability makes each threshold set finite.
Finite invariant weight truncations give the exponent-zero two-cluster bound, followed by the truncated-mean and square-root contraction.
A summable symmetric enumeration kernel has at least a fixed multiple of epsilon to the power minus 1/s edges above threshold.
Attach the unmarked branches of a spanning tree to the finite marked-core partition without changing its marked endpoint counts.
Count sufficiently heavy displacements on the positive-edge graph; translation mass transport and the tail exponent are explicit.

A general transfer is proved with arbitrary spatial-sum exponent gamma<d. It reuses the written two-ghost theorem, chooses the radius directly from n, and solves a finite least-amplitude quadratic. No imported two-ghost theorem is needed.
Combine marked-tree pieces across clusters and apply BK, then derive tails and moments at a real quantile.
Tail integration, Jensen, Hölder and Harris retain the dependence on all moment indices.
